appendixExamples.source: phase3/examples/results.json (WS-EX, DONE), RESULTS.md, REPORT.md; recomputed three-way analysis in examples-triple.json

X1.title: F32_MAX written into a 16-bit float storage texture (jump-flood-distance; per WS-EX also the suika-sdf distance texture): Metal/Lavapipe store 0x7bff (65504), SwiftShader NaN 0x7fff, then saturate(NaN)=0 turns the whole canvas navy vs cream
X1.kind: spec-indeterminate behaviour relied on by the example (backend-numerics difference in an unconstrained domain)
X1.oracle: WGSL 17.2 texel formats: write value of a 16float channel is quantizeToF16(T); quantizeToF16 (17.5.47): "If e is outside the finite range of binary16 ... the result is an indeterminate value" (shader-creation error only for const-expressions)
X1.note: Neither 65504 nor NaN is spec-violating; the example is non-portable. Local material is the WGSL spec only: a WebGPU-level clamp/inf rule for texture stores was not available here -> UNVERIFIED beyond WGSL. suika-sdf: the example dir has no F32_MAX literal (value may come from a library); cause taken from WS-EX, not re-verified.

X2.title: shader-f16 optional feature: Metal and Lavapipe take the f16 path, SwiftShader falls back to f32 (mnist-inference, monocular-light-injection; also log-test lines)
X2.oracle: none needed; WS-EX: with f16 hidden WGSL is identical on all backends for all 87 examples and mnist logits differ <= 4.6e-4 relative

X3.title: bitonic-sort: Lavapipe is the lone outlier (workload size derived from adapter limits)
X3.oracle: none (integer example; Phase-2 15-example run had it identical on all backends at the fixed test size)
X3.note: Per WS-EX the sizes come from the adapter limits; not re-verified here (hypothesis H7).

X4.title: prng-cpu-gpu / uniformity: BPETER PRNG = fract(cos(a)*136.8168): differs between ALL pairs (also Metal vs Lavapipe, 99.6% of words differ)
X4.kind: relies on an unconstrained domain: cos accuracy is defined only on [-pi, pi]; the factor 136.8 plus fract amplifies any cos difference (even in-domain, CTS allows +-5e-4 -> +-0.07 in the fract input)
X4.oracle: real CTS cosInterval: bounded only inside [-pi, pi], unbounded (indeterminate) for 100.123 and 12345.678 (E11)
X4.note: Integer PRNGs (xoroshiro, LCG) are bit-identical everywhere; the argument magnitude of BPETER in the example was not instrumented (hypothesis H8). uniformity: cause not isolated by WS-EX (sign-of-zero ruled out).

X5.title: chaotic amplification of last-bit differences in iterated simulations (3d-fish, attractors, compute-particles, slime-mold)
X5.kind: backend-numerics difference amplified by the example (hypothesis, WS-EX H1)
X5.oracle: none directly (no per-step reference); Metal~Lavapipe is already "large" for 3d-fish/attractors/compute-particles
X5.note: Would be settled by running 1-3 steps and comparing against an f64 model.

X6.title: SwiftShader lone outlier, small differences (tiny Metal~Lavapipe, small SS): react/confetti, react/spinning-triangle, cubemap-reflection, phong-reflection, ray-marching, stencil, vaporrave, boids, simulation/confetti, wind-map, sdf-docs-examples, threejs/varyings
X6.kind: backend-numerics difference inside spec (hypothesis: SwiftShader sin/cos/pow error G04, plus rasteriser/sampler differences for the 3-4 examples with no direct transcendental call)
X6.oracle: signature matches G04 (SwiftShader sin/cos error ~2e-4, Lavapipe = Metal) but no per-example oracle; static std usage: 9 of 12 call sin/cos/pow/exp/atan2 directly
X6.note: All have <1% of pixels differing by >2/255 (severity s) or tiny.

X7.title: repeat-to-repeat nondeterminism at cp3 on at least one backend: jelly-slider (SwiftShader), jelly-switch (Lavapipe, SwiftShader), compute-particles-snow (Metal) - async races/timers or chaotic state
X7.kind: example/test nondeterminism - cross-backend differences for these cannot be attributed to backends
X7.oracle: WS-EX determinism check (run1 vs run2 readbacks): see per-example flags

X8.title: remaining all-differ examples with small/moderate canvas/texture differences on every pair (rasterisation, transcendental and sampler last-bit differences)
